item.title: Anthropic’s IPO slide fuels fresh concerns over AI valuations; 37 stocks decline despite positive earnings multiples
item.description: Anthropic’s fall below its IPO price has intensified concerns over lofty AI valuations, even as earnings forecasts improve across the technology sector. Investors are increasingly focused on whether heavy spending can translate into durable profits.
item.dc:creator: ETMarkets.com
item.content:encoded: Anthropic shares dropping below its initial public offering price has intensified investor scrutiny of high technology valuations, as markets question whether even the biggest beneficiaries of the AI boom can generate enough profit to justify their share prices, Reuters reported.Shares of the Claude developer were trading near $80.50, below their $83 offer price and nearly 30% below their November 19 opening price.The swift reversal reflects growing unease over how much investors are willing to pay for future growth, even as earnings prospects improve for many companies benefiting from artificial intelligence.For live updates on US Markets, click hereOf the 86 Nasdaq-100 companies with positive earnings multiples and available revision data, 60 saw their forward 12-month earnings forecasts rise over the past three months, according to a Reuters analysis of LSEG data. Yet shares of 37 of those companies declined over the same period.Nvidia shares have fallen about 25% over the past three months despite a nearly 20% increase in earnings forecasts. Marvell Technology and Lumentum have each lost more than 40% of their market value, even as earnings estimates rose 15% and 20%, respectively.High expectationsDespite the selloff, valuation premiums remain substantial.The 25 most highly valued Nasdaq-100 companies, many with exposure to AI, autonomous driving and other emerging technologies, traded at a median 38 times projected earnings for the next 12 months. That compares with 18 times for the remaining companies with positive earnings multiples, Reuters calculations showed.Anthropic illustrates how much future growth is already reflected in technology valuations. Morningstar’s $92-per-share fair value estimate, just 12% above Anthropic’s latest closing price, assumes annual revenue will rise nearly sevenfold over the next five years.Morningstar’s estimates range from $25 to $188 a share under different scenarios, highlighting the sensitivity of Anthropic’s valuation to assumptions about future growth and profitability.The reassessment has been uneven across the sector. Forward price-to-earnings multiples for cybersecurity firms Fortinet and Palo Alto Networks rose the most over the past three months, climbing 11.5% and 10.8%, respectively. Multiples for Sandisk, Nvidia, Intuit and Analog Devices contracted the most, falling between 15% and 26%, LSEG data showed.Also Read: AI credit fears drive CoreWeave, Nvidia risk gauges to record highs“Investors pay up for earnings they believe will last and discount those they think will fade,” said Christopher Gannatti, global head of research at WisdomTree, according to Reuters.Gannatti contrasted Palantir’s high valuation with memory-chip maker Micron’s much lower multiple, arguing that high memory prices could spur additional supply and eventually weigh on prices and profits. Palantir trades at 65 times forward earnings, compared with 3.5 times for Micron, according to LSEG data.Growth spending adds to profit risksThe spending needed to deliver the growth implied by these valuations is another risk to future profitability.CoreWeave reported a 168% rise in third-quarter revenue to $3.66 billion and a contracted revenue backlog of $132.5 billion. Yet the AI computing provider recorded a net loss of $709 million and expects capital spending of $37 billion to $39 billion this year.“Technological breakthroughs don’t automatically translate into attractive returns on capital,” said Troy Hooper, co-head of equity capital markets for the Americas at Mergermarket, according to Reuters. “A year ago, investors were paying a much bigger premium for the promise of AI. Today, they’re getting more tangible evidence of that promise and are seeking stronger profits.”Hooper said increased competition could lower AI prices for customers, hurting companies investing heavily in the technology. Willis Tsai, head of global equities at Nuveen, said rising depreciation charges on AI chips and servers could pressure cloud companies’ margins even as demand for computing capacity grows.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

item.title: RBI net buyer of dollars for fourth straight month in September, data shows
item.description: The Reserve Bank of India recorded net purchases of $6.94 billion in the foreign exchange market during September. It bought a total of $82.18 billion while selling $75.25 billion in currency transactions. Despite a decline in the rupee, capital inflows reached about $143 billion due to various measures. Indian equities have recently attracted investors, leading to a rise in the rupee's value.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Reserve Bank of India was a net buyer in the foreign exchange market for the fourth consecutive month in September, reflecting likely interventions, swap maturities and absorption of capital inflows.The central bank bought a net $6.94 billion, with gross purchases of $82.18 billion and sales of $75.25 billion, according to data released on Wednesday in its monthly bulletin. It had purchased a net amount of $43.26 billion in August.The sustained buying comes as measures aimed at capital inflows drew about $143 billion, mostly from a zero-cost hedging facility for banks' overseas FX deposits. The inflows came despite the rupee slipping 0.7% in September on elevated crude prices and surging global bond yields.The bank's net outstanding forward dollar sales stood at nearly $240 billion as of end-September, compared with $200 billion at the end of August.The picture has shifted meaningfully since then, with Indian equities in November attracting investors fleeing AI-driven markets and oil prices dropping, accelerating a sharp reversal in the currency's fortunes.On Wednesday, the Indian rupee rose 0.73% against the US dollar to 92.23, climbing to its highest level so far this financial year.
